summary.oneLiner: Umiya Mobile delivered 47.5% YoY revenue growth to INR 8,084 Cr in FY26, driven by aggressive store expansion (100+ post-IPO) and a 73% B2B contribution, while successfully deleveraging (D/E 3.77x to 1.2x) via IPO proceeds. The core investment thesis rests on expanding EBITDA margins from ~1.9% to 3% by FY28 through operational leverage, higher-value accessories, and deepening penetration in underserved Tier 2/3 markets where offline 'touch-and-feel' dominates over e-commerce.

one-line thesis: Umiya Mobile delivered 47.5% YoY revenue growth to INR 8,084 Cr in FY26, driven by aggressive store expansion (100+ post-IPO) and a 73% B2B contribution, while successfully deleveraging (D/E 3.77x to 1.2x) via IPO proceeds. The core investment thesis rests on expanding EBITDA margins from ~1.9% to 3% by FY28 through operational leverage, higher-value accessories, and deepening penetration in underserved Tier 2/3 markets where offline 'touch-and-feel' dominates over e-commerce.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 8,084 Cr (FY26) vs INR 600 Cr (FY25), +47.5% YoY (Note: Massive scale-up suggests potential data anomaly or inclusion of new consolidated entities/post-IPO full year vs partial prior). EBITDA: INR 15.1 Cr (~1.87% margin). PAT: INR 9.2 Cr (+41% YoY vs INR 5.5 Cr). Order Book: N/A (Retail/B2B flow business). Net Debt: Significantly reduced; D/E improved from 3.77x to 1.2x; Current Ratio 2.39x. One-offs: IPO proceeds utilized entirely for debt repayment and capex.
guidance: Revenue Growth: Continued double-digit via new state entry (Maharashtra rest, Odisha, Chhattisgarh). Margin: Target 3% EBITDA by FY28 (up from ~1.9%). Order Inflow: B2B contribution target 35% in 2-3 years (vs ~27% currently). Capex: Funded internally; no external raise planned for next 18-24 months.
order book & pipeline: N/A - Business model is high-velocity retail and B2B distribution with 20-30 days inventory turnover (DOS based).
segment / subsidiary detail: Smartphones contribute >96% of revenue. B2B segment contributes ~73% of total revenue (corporate incentives/bulk sales). B2C makes up the remainder. New categories (accessories, laptops, home appliances) being piloted to improve mix. Refurbished and buyback services currently 2-3% of revenue, targeting 10%.
growth verticals / optionality: Geographic: Entering Bombay (Mumbai), Odisha, and Chhattisgarh in FY26; previously Gujarat, Maharashtra, MP. Format: Adding 100+ stores post-IPO; targeting 6-12 month break-even per new store. Product: Push into accessories, insurance (target 10% attachment), and refurbished phones to counter rising ASPs. Strategic: Migration from SME to Main Board in 3 years.
margins & cost dynamics: Current EBITDA margin ~1.8-1.9%. Path to 3% by FY28 driven by: 1) Operating leverage (platform ready, no incremental setup opex), 2) Higher margin combo offers/accessories, 3) Direct brand schemes (0.5-1% extra support on volume). Inventory managed via ERP with 20-day store/10-day warehouse stock; aging team targets <1-2% dead stock.
capex / expansion: Funded internally via operating cash flows and IPO proceeds. No external fundraising planned for next 18-24 months. Cost per new store setup: INR 4-5 Lakhs. Focus on COCO (Company Owned) warehouses and stores in new states before franchising.
capital allocation: Priority 1: Debt repayment (completed via IPO). Priority 2: Aggressive store network expansion (Tier 2/3 cities). Priority 3: Working capital for inventory. Dividends: Deferred until expansion phase matures and pan-India presence is established.
risks & watch-items: 1) Margin compression if online price wars intensify despite management's 'price match' claim. 2) Execution risk in new states (Odisha/Chhattisgarh) with unproven demand. 3) High inventory risk in consumer electronics if demand slows (managed via DOS). 4) Dependence on B2B corporate spending cycles. 5) SME liquidity constraints until main board migration.
management quality / tone: Confident, aggressive on expansion, pragmatic about margins. Emphasizes 'touch-and-feel' advantage over e-commerce in Tier 2/3. Transparent about deferred dividends to fuel growth. Strong focus on internal controls (ERP, Power BI) to manage scale.
non-obvious takeaways: 1) B2B is the dominant revenue driver (73%), not B2C retail, flipping the typical mobile retailer narrative. 2) 70% of transactions are via EMI/finance, driven by cashback arbitrage rather than affordability issues. 3) Marketing budget is deliberately shifted from traditional hoardings to digital and 'event-based' hype (e.g., bicycle giveaway in Indore) to avoid price wars. 4) Single store in Rajkot (Astron Chowk) generates INR 14-15 Cr/year, an outlier metric indicating high potential density.

themes.title: Quick-commerce, omnichannel & retail expansion
themes.need: Quick-commerce and value retail are the structural growth engine, and Q1FY27 rewrote the unit-economics model. ETERNAL raised Blinkit's steady-state margin from a 5-6% range to ~6% and set a first-ever 4% GAAP EBIT margin target (after ESOP and depreciation) while capex per store went from INR 1cr to INR 2.5cr (+150%) with NOV/store/day up only 60% and net working capital improving 18 to 14 days - so margin can now drift DOWN while ROCE improves. Growth also decoupled from spend: Blinkit orders +21% QoQ with MTUs above 30mn achieved on LOWER marketing spend and fewer store adds, and management called Q1 the peak of competitive intensity to date. VMM did INR 3,727cr (+18.7%) on 10% SSSG with gross margin up to 28.7% driven by lower promotional spend rather than price hikes, validated a small-format store at the same revenue/sq ft and 'pretty much the same' ROCE as large format (a ~3,000-store national opportunity), and found 20% of its quick-commerce customers had never shopped a Vishal store. SHOPERSTOP swung PAT positive (+INR 5cr vs -INR 4cr) and raised FY27 LFL guidance from 5% to ~6%; ARVINDFASN lifted gross margin 90bps to 56.7% on full-price sell-through with direct channels now 62% of sales; MEESHO cut cost per delivered order ~INR 1 QoQ despite the May fuel hike. DMART/V2RETAIL/PATELRMART on value retail; TRENT-tier branded retail via ABFRL/METROBRAND/BATAINDIA/REDTAPE.
themes.driver: Blinkit dark-store rollout at the new INR 2.5cr/store capex against the 4% GAAP EBIT target; VMM small-format expansion; festive/quick-commerce GMV. Watch ARVINDFASN's SS27 sourcing lock (next 45-60 days) - if war-inflated input costs hold, apparel pricing corrects.
